source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Recurrent episodes of eating unusually large amounts with loss of control and distress, without compensatory behavior or a persistently low body weight.","B":"Markedly restricted intake, intense fear of gaining weight, low body weight, distorted body image, and denial of the seriousness of low weight.","C":"Recurrent binge eating followed by self-induced vomiting or laxative use while body weight may remain in an expected or higher range.","D":"Restricted intake driven by food texture, sensory features, or fear of choking without a primary fear of weight gain or distorted body image."}}
source_row.rationale: Anorexia nervosa is characterized by severe restriction, intense fear of weight gain, low body weight, distorted body image, and often denial of the seriousness of low weight. Option B is correct. Option A better resembles binge-eating disorder. Option C describes a binge-purge pattern consistent with bulimia nervosa. Option D better resembles ARFID, where restriction is not primarily driven by weight-gain fear or distorted body image.
source_row.source_detail: NIMH — Eating Disorders: What You Need to Know, Anorexia Nervosa: severe restriction of food intake, intense fear of gaining weight/behaviors interfering with weight gain, significantly low body weight/extreme thinness, distorted body image and lack of recognition/denial of the seriousness of low weight are characteristic features. Current NIMH eating-disorders publication live-rechecked 2026-08-15; difficulty corrected to easy because the item is direct syndrome recognition with clearly differentiated eating-disorder distractors.
